title: Hell
definition: Hell is the final state of conscious judgment and separation from God's favorable presence for those who remain in rebellion against Him.
summary: Hell is the righteous judgment of God against sin and unbelief.
christFocus: Jesus warned about hell with seriousness and gave Himself so sinners might be rescued from judgment.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Hell is a sobering doctrine. It is not a joke, metaphor for inconvenience, or tool for manipulation. Scripture presents hell as real judgment against sin and rebellion.

God's judgment is righteous. Hell shows that sin against the holy God is serious and that evil will not be excused forever. Jesus Himself spoke clearly and soberly about judgment.

This doctrine must be handled with tears, reverence, and Gospel urgency. The purpose is not fear tactics but faithful warning and earnest proclamation of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people either deny hell or speak of it carelessly. Hell matters because it reveals the seriousness of sin, the justice of God, and the urgency of the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let this doctrine humble you, not harden you. Pray for the lost, proclaim Christ clearly, and flee to the Savior who rescues sinners from judgment.
